title: fix(components,schema-catalog): button-group honors per-button `disabled`, corpus stops authoring 29 unread keys
body:
Fixes #7077

Executes the maintainer ruling of 2026-09-04 (decision batch #25, option 2), recorded in [comment 5534409692](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/7077#issuecomment-5534409692). Not re-adjudicated here.

Clause-②: no — re-judged from the actual diff, not from the expectation. The diff touches `packages/components`, `examples/schema-catalog` and one `.mdx`; it touches **no** `packages/types` file and **no** zod mirror. Forwarding an already-declared key to the DOM changes no accept/refuse behaviour and widens no public surface, and the fixture edits are corpus, not contract.

## ⚠️ One row of the ruling is stale — `onClick` is NOT wired, and that is not a gap

The ruling's item 2 says to wire "the two keys `ButtonGroupButton` already declares". On `main` today only **one** of them is declared. `onClick` was RETIRED by **#7339** (landed 2026-09-02, `a8d5c717e`, implementing #6124 under the same ADR-0049) and now refuses by name in all three carriers:

| carrier | state on `main` |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/types/src/navigation.ts` | `onClick?: never;` tagged `RETIRED (objectui#6124, ADR-0049)` |
| `packages/types/src/zod/navigation.zod.ts:148` | `onClick: handlerKeyRefusal('onClick', 'retired', 'Click handler')` |
| `content/docs/components/basic/button-group.mdx:29` | already teaches the `never` row |

The card was filed 2026-08-31, before that landed; triage verified the renderer file only and carried the stale reading into the ruling. Wiring `onClick` would be an **un-retirement** of a key another landed ADR-0049 ruling deliberately killed — an edit to `packages/types` plus the mirror plus the docs, which is a contract widening and would flip Clause-② to `yes`. That is not the lane's to do.

⭐ **The ruling's intent is already satisfied for `onClick` by the other route.** ADR-0049 is enforce-**or**-remove; #6124 removed it. There is no declared-but-dead handler left to forward. This needs PM acknowledgement, not new work.

## Re-count on the current tree — matches the card exactly

| fixture | `buttons[].value` | `buttons[].icon` | group `value` | `selectionMode` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `basic-button-group.json` | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `icon-toolbar.json` | 3 | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| `multiple-selection.json` | 3 | 3 | 1 | 1 |
| `outline-variant.json` | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `single-selection.json` | 3 | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| `with-icons.json` | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| **total** | **17** | **8** | **2** | **2** |

**29, six of six — no drift from the 2026-08-31 table.** 25 leave by being stripped, 4 by `with-icons.json` being removed. No fixture authored `onClick`.

## What changed

**Renderer** — `packages/components/src/renderers/basic/button-group.tsx` gains exactly one line, `disabled={button.disabled}`, matching every sibling that declares item-level `disabled` (`tabs`, `select`, `dropdown-menu`, `menubar`, `context-menu`, `toggle-group` since #4632). #4632 is the precedent in shape as well as spelling: same finding, `icon` retired and `disabled` wired.

**Corpus** — all 29 keys gone. `button-group` stays presentational.

**The two filename traps the ruling named:**

- **`icon-toolbar.json` — the blank-button trap is STALE and does not fire.** #5931's "renders three buttons with empty text and zero svg" was measured before **#6318**, which gave it labels (that PR's own changelog: "the button group's three buttons went from blank to labelled"). Verified by rendering, not by assuming — see below. It keeps its labels and its `variant: outline` / `size: sm` demo, so "rewritten with labels" is already satisfied and the file stays.
- **`with-icons.json` — REMOVED.** With `icon` retired it authored no icons, and what remained duplicated `basic-button-group.json`. Its demo slot on the docs page goes with it.

**Rendered output of every surviving fixture**, read rather than assumed (`catalog-gallery-render.test.tsx` fails only on an unregistered type, so it renders blanks green):

```
basic-button-group.json  buttons=3  texts=["Left","Center","Right"]        svg=0
icon-toolbar.json        buttons=3  texts=["Copy","Cut","Paste"]           svg=0
multiple-selection.json  buttons=3  texts=["Bold","Italic","Underline"]    svg=0
outline-variant.json     buttons=3  texts=["Day","Week","Month"]           svg=0
single-selection.json    buttons=3  texts=["Option 1","Option 2","Option 3"] svg=0
```

No blank buttons. `svg=0` is unchanged by this PR — the renderer never read `icon` in the first place.

**Docs delta is only what the fixture set forces.** #6347 already removed `value` / `selectionMode` / `onValueChange` / `icon` from the page; re-measured on `main` and nothing else remained to delete. The page loses the `with-icons` example, and the `DemoGrid` wrapper plus its now-unused import go with it.

## Two landed pins my change moves, updated rather than deleted

- `safe-validate-corpus-6318.test.ts` asserted `buttons.map(b => b.icon)` was `['copy','scissors','clipboard']`. That pin's own header says it names the key that moved precisely so a later sweep deleting it cannot go silently green — this PR is that sweep. The assertion is **inverted, not removed**: it now asserts `icon` and `value` are absent, and the `label` assertion (#6318's actual repair) is untouched.
- `button-group-doc-surface-6347.test.ts` asserts `single-selection.json` and `multiple-selection.json` stay **on disk**. They do: keys stripped, files kept. See the open question below.

## New pins

- `packages/components/src/__tests__/button-group-item-disabled-7077.test.tsx` — asserts the rendered `button` elements, not the schema. A test asserting `disabled` is a member of the mirror would restate a declaration this PR did not change and would stay green with the forwarding deleted again.
- `examples/schema-catalog/test/button-group-retired-keys-7077.test.ts` — derives "undeclared" from the shipped mirror rather than blacklisting the four names, so the rule is "author nothing undeclared" and keeps holding as the mirror moves. Carries a counter-probe asserting the retired keys really do parse green through `BaseSchema.passthrough()`, which is why membership is not read off parse.

## Ablation — both legs, mutation and restore proved by state

Subject resolves through a relative **source** import (`../renderers`), not through package `exports` to `dist`, so no rebuild leg applies — and the RED below is itself the proof: a dist-resolved subject would have ignored the source mutation and stayed green.

```
HEAD_BLOB=67d1ef545fa58e2c46d52ad18856d762a801b385
MUTATION: anchored delete applied (1 occurrence)
MUT_PROOF: anchored_count_after=0 (expect 0)  MUT_BLOB=3f50669992c157e160e624350d7810f1c061e210
MUTATED_LEG_EXIT=1     Tests  2 failed | 2 passed (4)
                       expect(element).toBeDisabled()  line 65  ('Cut')
                       expect(element).toBeDisabled()  line 82  ('Right')
RESTORE_PROOF: blob=67d1ef545... head=67d1ef545... diff_empty=yes anchored_count=1
RESTORED_LEG_EXIT=0    Tests  4 passed (4)
```

Predicted direction RED, observed RED. Mutation proved on disk (anchored count 1 to 0, blob differs from HEAD) **before** any result was read; restore via `git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH` and proved **by state** — blob equal to HEAD's and `git diff HEAD` empty — not by exit code. Whole run under `trap restore EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths. Exactly 2 of 4 cases failed under mutation: the two that assert the forwarding. The two that assert "no button disabled when none declares it" correctly stayed green, which is what makes the RED specific rather than a broken render.

## Verification — all at final commit `17beb3d3e`, tree clean

| run | result |
| --- | --- |
| `vitest run packages/components/` | **231 files / 2159 tests passed** |
| `vitest run examples/schema-catalog/` + the three `packages/types` button-group pins | **30 files / 2167 tests passed** |
| `type-check` (components, schema-catalog) | exit 0, both echo `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` |
| `lint` (components, schema-catalog) | exit 0, **0 errors** |
| `check:doc-snippets` | "Every covered documentation snippet compiles against the built types." 452 of 452 judged, 0 failed |
| `check:sdui-registration-pins` | "All 16 registration(s) a `sideEffects` array promises are present in the built console (518 chunks weighed)" |
| `check:icon-record-names` | "OK — 182 authored/declared names reaching 1 record-reading resolver are live `icons` keys" |
| `check:doc-types` · `check:doc-fences` · `check:control-bytes` · `check:docs-route-closure` | exit 0 |
| `regenerate:check` | "index.ts is up to date (431 entries)" |

Both gates that first returned **exit 2 / PRECONDITION NOT MET** were treated as *not measured*, not as green: their prerequisites were built and both were re-run to a real verdict. The `check:sdui-registration-pins` prerequisite additionally required building `@object-ui/plugin-tree`, whose absence is pre-existing and unrelated to this diff.

Type-check genuinely covers the new tests: both `tsconfig.test.json` projects' `include` globs (`src/**/*.test.tsx`, `test/**/*.test.ts`) match the new files.

## Open question for the maintainer — filenames that outlive the capability

`single-selection.json` and `multiple-selection.json` now author no selection, but their **filenames** still name the capability this ruling declares does not exist, and the corpus is retrieved by name. That is the same class as the `with-icons.json` trap the ruling named. I did **not** act on it: the ruling gave no instruction for these two, and `button-group-doc-surface-6347.test.ts` explicitly asserts both stay on disk ("catalog entries are a separate verification population and are NOT deleted to tidy that up"). Deleting or renaming them means editing another card's landed pin, which is a decision rather than a dev's call. After stripping, both are structurally identical to `basic-button-group.json` and differ only in labels.
